q6.answer: The Order service moves a checkout forward: it calls Inventory to reserve and claim, publishes ChargeRequested, and reacts to PaymentSucceeded/PaymentDeclined. The record of progress is the order's saved status in Order's own database (PLACED, AWAITING_PAYMENT, PAID, CONFIRMED, etc.), and a recovery loop in Order re-drives orders stuck in PLACED or PAID.

q7.answer: The provider calls the webhook HTTP endpoint on Payment, which maps the provider payment reference to the order id, saves the outcome and publishes a PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined event through the outbox on the broker. Order consumes that event and finishes the order.

q8.answer: Payment stores each provider event id in a processed-events table with a unique constraint; a repeat finds the id, replies 200 and does nothing. Downstream, consumers are idempotent: each handler checks the order's current status before acting, so repeated events have no extra effect.

q9.answer: On PaymentDeclined, Order marks PAYMENT_DECLINED, tells the customer, and sends a ReleaseHold event to Inventory. Inventory releases the hold (status RELEASED) only if it is still HELD, so the stock returns to sale at once; otherwise it does nothing.

q10.answer: Order marks the order PAID and asks Inventory to claim the hold; Inventory grants it only if the hold is still HELD and its expiry time has not passed (conditional status update, so claim and expiry cannot both win). If refused, Order cancels as out of stock, emails the customer and requests a full refund. The hold is strict: any success after 10 minutes goes to refund, even if the stock is still unsold.

q11.answer: Payment saves the refund row as REQUESTED before calling the provider; a failure or timeout moves it to RETRYING and a retry job repeats with backoff using the stable key refund-order id. After N attempts it becomes REFUND_FAILED, raises an ops alert and stays in the retry list, retried daily. The pending refund is tracked in Payment's own database; Order does not track it. N is not set.

q12.answer: When the claim succeeds, Order marks CONFIRMED and publishes OrderConfirmed with order id and cart id; the Cart service consumes that event and empties that cart, and only then.
